sentences.text: Ceramornis was a genus of ornithuran dinosaurs living in the Late Cretaceous.
The single known species, Ceramornis major, is known only from a small fragment of a coracoid bone.
Because the fossil material is so limited, scientists cannot fully determine its exact place in the evolutionary tree.
Remains were found at the Lull 2 site within the Lance Formation of Niobrara County, Wyoming.
A research team from the University of California collected the specimen UCMP V53957 in 1958.
It belongs to the family Cimolopterygidae, which also includes the genera Cimolopteryx and Lamarqueavis.
Some researchers have suggested this family might be related to the modern bird order Charadriiformes based on bone structure.
These animals lived between 72.2 and 66 million years ago during the Maastrichtian stage.
This time period occurred just before the major extinction event that ended the Cretaceous.
It remains unclear whether the bird order Charadriiformes was already a distinct group during the Maastrichtian.
